summary: Target-level geometric refinement of the accepted RS.2 plan: coherent native root systems, factorial reindexing, normalized coframe torsors and their fpqc limit, the infinite quotient, and the DVR residual gerbe with Kummer coordinates. The accepted affine algebra and Spec calculations are imported. The independent review added the limit theorem for towers of finite flat torsors, which no supplier states, and re-pointed the descent, quotient, Picard-groupoid, finite-root-stack and Kummer contracts to the SchemeAndStackFoundations roadmap merged into TauCetiRoadmap on 14 October 2026. All geometric carriers and proofs remain unchecked; complete means the planning pass is complete, not that RS.2 is mathematically closed.

nodes.title: Native root transition pseudodiagram
nodes.statement: For a scheme X with invertible sheaf L and section s, form the root-groupoid diagram indexed by positive integers with the arrow m→n when n divides m. At T→X, F(n,m) sends (M,t,φ) to (M^(m/n),t^(m/n),φ), using the specified tensor-power comparison to interpret φ. On arrows it takes tensor powers. Supply unit constraints and composition isomorphisms F(n,m)F(m,l)≅F(n,l), including their coherence and compatibility with arbitrary scheme pullback.
hypotheses: Native finite root groupoids from RS.0–RS.1, using the core of InvertibleSheaf, not its full category.
One fixed coefficient universe and explicitly lifted object/morphism universes; no same-universe assertion for all schemes.
proofSteps: Take the tensor-power functor and its section comparison supplied by RS.0 and SF.3. Transport the root equation through the associativity comparison.
Construct each compositor from the specified power associativity isomorphism. Its root-section equation and arrow naturality follow from the corresponding RS.0 laws.

Use the unit and associativity coherence of those same comparisons to obtain the pseudodiagram laws. Finite pullback comparisons induce a strong transformation of diagrams, including its modification laws.

Under the comparison of the RS.0–RS.1 native root groupoids with rootStack n (L,s) of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21, each F(n,m) is that roadmap's rootStack.transition. §1.21 states the transition maps only; the unit and compositor constraints, their coherence and their pullback modifications are the RS.2 content of this node.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.2 and the paragraph preceding it, p.13
sources.match: Transitions and composition in the monoidal-functor model motivate this native line-bundle specialization. Strict equality in that model is not imposed on tensor powers.
The objects and arrows retain the section and the power identification.

acceptance: For n|m|l and a root (M,t,φ), the compositor F(n,m)F(m,l)(M,t,φ) ≅ F(n,l)(M,t,φ) is the tensor-power associativity isomorphism (M^(l/m))^(m/n) ≅ M^(l/n) assembled from InvertibleSheaf.tensorProductAssoc and the unit isomorphisms; for n = m = l it is the unit constraint.
On objects and arrows each F(n,m) agrees with rootStack.transition of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21.
On the zero-section root (O,0,id) of exponent 6 over T, F(2,6) sends the automorphism ζ ∈ μ6(T) to ζ³ ∈ μ2(T).

nodes.title: Coherent native root systems
nodes.statement: Specialize the imported compatible-family carrier to the native root pseudodiagram. A system over T consists of roots x_n and specified isomorphisms α(n,m):F(n,m)(x_m)≅x_n for every n|m. For n|m|l, α(n,m) composed with F(n,m)(α(m,l)) equals α(n,l) after the compositor; the unit equation uses the unit constraint. Arrows h are component root isomorphisms satisfying h_n α(n,m)=α′(n,m)F(n,m)(h_m). Pullback acts on components and comparisons. This groupoid, not a set of root classes, is the infinite-root fibre.
hypotheses: The pseudodiagram and universe policy of transition-native.
All components are actual root objects with their sections and power identifications.
proofSteps: Instantiate the generic compatible-family construction with the positive-divisibility root diagram.
Use the generic componentwise category structure and invertibility criterion, since every fibre arrow is already an isomorphism.
Construct scheme pullback from the strong transformation supplied by transition-native; evaluation and the section/power equations remain componentwise.

sources.match: The infinite root stack is a genuine two-limit. The displayed cocycle presentation specializes that limit to roots of one pair.

acceptance: If s is invertible on X, the groupoid of systems over every T→X is contractible.
For X = Spec k and (L,s) = (O,0), the system (O,0,id)_n with identity transitions has automorphism group lim μ_n(T) over T; over T = Spec ℝ this group is trivial.
A family of root triples with pairwise isomorphisms that violates the 1|2|4 cocycle is not an object, even when every finite isomorphism class is correct.

nodes.title: Factorial reindexing of native roots
nodes.statement: Restriction of coherent native root systems to the sequence 1!,2!,3!,… is an equivalence of groupoids, pseudonatural in T→X and compatible with all positive-degree evaluations up to specified natural isomorphism. The inverse extends both objects and arrows and supplies all transition cocycles. The same argument applies to coherent finite torsor systems.
hypotheses: The native root pseudodiagram; the factorial sequence starts at 1.
Use cofinality of positive divisibility, not a bijection of index sets.
proofSteps: For an n-component choose a factorial r! divisible by n (n | r! once r ≥ n, Nat.dvd_factorial) and apply F(n,r!) to the r!-component. For comparing n|m, compare their chosen stages in a common larger factorial (r! | s! for r ≤ s, Nat.factorial_dvd_factorial).
Compose the supplied factorial transition isomorphisms and pseudodiagram compositors. Their cocycles show independence of the common comparison stage and give the all-positive cocycle.

Extend component arrows in the same way. Build the restriction–extension unit and counit from the original transitions; verify their naturality, triangle identities and pullback modifications. No uniqueness claim discards stabilizer arrows.

sources.match: The source permits cofinal indexing. The extension of native tensor-power objects, arrows and cocycles is the explicit root-specific proof obligation here.

acceptance: The inverse is a groupoid equivalence with evaluation comparisons; an inverse limit of sets does not meet this target.
The unit of the equivalence at degree 5 is the given isomorphism α(5,5!): F(5,5!)(x_(5!)) ≅ x_5.
For (L,s) = (O,0), restriction induces an isomorphism lim_n μ_n(T) ≅ lim_r μ_(r!)(T) on automorphism groups of the trivial system.

nodes.title: Effective fpqc descent for native root systems
nodes.statement: The native compatible-root pseudofunctor is an fpqc stack. A descent datum consists of a compatible root system on a cover, with compatible-system arrows on overlaps satisfying their cocycle. Descending all finite roots and all α produces the descended system, and descent on compatible arrows is fully faithful.
hypotheses: Use the fpqc topology on schemes over X and the existing finite-root fpqc descent theorem.
No finite-presentation or algebraicity assertion for the infinite stack.
proofSteps: Apply the imported compatible-limit stack descent theorem to the finite-root stack diagram.
Effectiveness descends each x_n. Full faithfulness descends α(n,m) and the system arrows. Equality of their coherence diagrams is detected on the cover.
Use the supplied pullback constraints to compare the descended system with the original descent datum. The fppf stack restriction follows because fppf covers are fpqc.

sources.match: The quotient uses actual fpqc torsors. Native effectivity is supplied by the imported finite and compatible-limit descent contracts.

acceptance: Twisting: over X = Spec ℚ with (L,s) = (O,0), descending the trivial system along the fpqc covering P → Spec ℚ of RS.2/roots-two-fpqc-native, with descent datum given by the G-action, yields a system x_P with Isom(x, x_P) ≅ P. It has no ℚ-rational isomorphism to x and is not isomorphic to x over any nonempty fppf ℚ-scheme, so an fppf stack would miss it.
Two system arrows that agree after pullback to an fpqc covering are equal.

nodes.title: Arbitrary base change of native infinite roots
nodes.statement: For g:Y→X, roots of (g*L,g*s) form a stack equivalent to the two-fibre product of the native infinite root stack of (L,s) with Y over X. The equivalence is compatible with every finite evaluation, all α, factorial restriction, and composites of base changes.
hypotheses: Arbitrary scheme morphisms, including nonflat maps.
Use the generic two-fibre products of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18 on the fpqc site, and the finite root base-change equivalences.
proofSteps: Apply the finite base-change equivalence to each root triple and to each component arrow.
The transition/pullback comparison transports every α and its cocycle. Construct the inverse by the inverse finite comparisons.
Check unit/counit and composition as modifications after each evaluation, using componentwise arrow extensionality. This makes no claim that arbitrary coefficient change is faithful.

sources.match: Finite and infinite roots commute with base change; the target records the native groupoid comparisons and their coherence.

acceptance: Along the closed point Spec k → Spec R of a DVR, the infinite root stack of (O(D),1) base changes to that of (N,0), N = O(D)|k; on the uniformizer chart this is C_R(π) ⊗_R k ≅ C_k(0) = colim k[z_n]/(z_n^n), with the nonzero nilpotent z_n retained.
For composable g: Y → X and h: Z → Y, the equivalence for gh is the composite of those for g and h up to the pullback compositors, checked after every finite evaluation.

nodes.title: Normalized coframes of a finite root
nodes.statement: For a root (M,t,φ:M^n≅O_T) of (O_T,f), let P_n be the sheaf of coframes β:M≅O_T with β^n=φ. This sheaf is represented by a finite locally free μn-torsor of rank n. Use LEFT action ζ·β=ζβ. The coordinate x_n(β)=β(t) satisfies x_n^n=f and x_n(ζ·β)=ζ x_n(β). Root isomorphisms act by β↦β h^−1. This is the normalized coframe torsor; the chart t^n=f itself is a torsor only when f is a unit.
hypotheses: A positive n, arbitrary scheme T, actual invertible sheaf and root section.
The target line has been trivialized; gluing for a general L uses root-limit-descent-native.
proofSteps: Choose a Zariski local basis of M. If φ of its nth power is the unit a, normalized coframes are given by an invertible coefficient b with b^n=a.

Globally P_n is the relative spectrum over T of the O_T-algebra ⊕_(0≤i<n) M^(⊗i), with multiplication M^(⊗i) ⊗ M^(⊗j) → M^(⊗(i+j)) followed by φ in degrees ≥ n (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.1 relative Spec). It is finite locally free of rank n, locally O_T[b]/(b^n − a), and it is the μ_n-torsor attached to the pair (M,φ) in the description of H¹_fppf(T,μ_n) by line bundles with a trivialized nth power (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11; Stacks Lemma 59.28.5, tag 040Q). No gluing beyond relative Spec is needed, and n need not be invertible.

Evaluate t in the normalized coframe. The root equation gives x_n^n=f; scaling the coframe gives the LEFT scaling convention. Transport along a root arrow preserves normalization and the evaluation map.

sources.match: Finite line-root and root-with-section presentations yield this normalized coframe specialization; no nonvanishing section is assumed.
The quotient requires a torsor and an equivariant chart map as distinct pieces of data.
The fppf H¹ of μ_n is the group of pairs of a line bundle and a trivialization of its nth power; the coframe torsor is the torsor attached to (M,φ).

acceptance: In a local basis e with φ(e^n) = a, P_n is Spec O_T[b]/(b^n − a) with a a unit, whether or not f vanishes, and the coordinate is x_n = b·c where t = c·e.
For the zero root (O,0,id), P_n is μ_n itself, while the chart fibre Spec k[z]/(z^n) is not a torsor for n > 1.

The coframe coordinates construct the equivariant infinite chart map.

nodes.title: Finite transition torsors of a coherent root
nodes.statement: For a coherent root system of (O_T,f) and n|m with q=m/n, the map P_m→P_n sends β_m to β_m^q α(n,m)^−1. It is equivariant for μm→μn, ζ↦ζ^q, and is a torsor under its kernel μq, finite locally free of rank q. These maps satisfy composition exactly after the chosen root coherence and are compatible with arbitrary base change and root-system arrows.
hypotheses: The normalized coframe convention, actual α(n,m), arbitrary characteristic and positive indices.
proofSteps: Normalization follows from α preserving the nth-power identification. Its section equation gives x_n=x_m^q.
Over P_n, choose a coframe of M_m locally and solve the qth-root equation for the required unit coefficient. This gives a finite flat μq-torsor; finite Kummer exactness supplies local surjectivity.
Compute compositions using the α cocycle and the tensor-power compositor, including the unit case. The same calculation respects root arrows and pullback.

sources.match: Compatible trivializations of rational-power data give the transition torsors. The finite coframe formula is the native one-pair specialization.

acceptance: For the trivial system (O,0,id)_n with identity transitions, P_m → P_n is μ_m → μ_n, ζ ↦ ζ^(m/n), a μ_(m/n)-torsor.
For the system of roots of 2 over ℚ, P_4 → P_2 is Spec ℚ[z_4]/(z_4^4 − 2) → Spec ℚ[z_2]/(z_2^2 − 2), z_2 ↦ z_4², finite locally free of rank 2.
The maps compose exactly: P_l → P_m → P_n equals P_l → P_n, using the α cocycle and the tensor-power compositor.

nodes.title: Limits of finite flat torsor towers
nodes.statement: Let T be a scheme. Let G_n (n ≥ 1) be commutative group schemes over T, each finite locally free, with homomorphisms π(n,m): G_m → G_n for n|m such that π(n,n) is the identity, π(n,m)π(m,l) = π(n,l), and each π(n,m) is faithfully flat with finite locally free kernel. Put G = lim G_n, an affine flat group scheme over T. Let P_n be fppf G_n-torsors with π(n,m)-equivariant T-morphisms p(n,m): P_m → P_n, p(n,n) = id and p(n,m)p(m,l) = p(n,l). Then: (a) each p(n,m) is a torsor under ker π(n,m), hence finite locally free and surjective; (b) the limit P = lim P_n exists, is affine over T, and over an affine open U ⊆ T its coordinate ring is the directed colimit of those of the P_n|U; (c) P → T is faithfully flat, so {P → T} is an fpqc covering; (d) the action map G ×_T P → P ×_T P, (g,x) ↦ (gx,x), is an isomorphism, so P is an fpqc G-torsor, and for every n the G-map P → P_n induces an isomorphism P ×^G G_n ≅ P_n of G_n-torsors; (e) formation of P commutes with every base change T′ → T; (f) G-equivariant T-morphisms P → Q between two such limits correspond bijectively to compatible families of G_n-equivariant morphisms P_n → Q_n; (g) for every fpqc G-torsor Q the pushforwards Q_n = Q ×^G G_n are fppf G_n-torsors and the canonical map Q → lim Q_n is an isomorphism. Hence fpqc G-torsors and such towers, with equivariant maps, form equivalent groupoids. Neither finite presentation of P nor fppf-local triviality of P is asserted.
hypotheses: T is an arbitrary scheme; the index set is the positive integers ordered by divisibility, which is directed.

Each G_n is finite locally free over T and each transition G_m → G_n is faithfully flat with finite locally free kernel. For G_n = μ_n,T and ζ ↦ ζ^(m/n) the transition is the qth-power map, q = m/n: the coordinate ring of μ_m is free of rank q over that of μ_n, and the kernel is μ_q.
Each P_n is an fppf G_n-torsor; the tower maps are equivariant and compose exactly.
proofSteps: (a) Fppf locally on T choose a section of P_m, so P_m ≅ G_m; then p(n,m) becomes π(n,m) followed by a translation of G_n. π(n,m) is finite, flat and of finite presentation with kernel K = ker π(n,m), and G_m ×_(G_n) G_m ≅ G_m × K, so it is a K-torsor. These properties are fpqc local on the base (Stacks 02KY, 02L2, 02LA).

(b) The transition maps are finite, hence affine, and P_1 is finite over T, so the limit exists and is computed affine-locally (merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9 affine_transition_limits; Stacks 01YW, 01YX). Over U = Spec R it is Spec of the directed colimit of the coordinate rings of the P_n|U.

(c) Each P_n|U is finite locally free and surjective over U, so its coordinate ring is a faithfully flat R-algebra; a directed colimit of faithfully flat R-algebras is faithfully flat (Stacks 090N). Translate with flat_and_surjective_iff_faithfullyFlat_of_isAffine. P is affine over T, hence quasi-compact, and {P → T} is an fpqc covering.

(d) Fibre products commute with limits: G ×_T P = lim(G_n ×_T P_n) and P ×_T P = lim(P_n ×_T P_n), and the action map is the limit of the finite action isomorphisms. The G-map P → P_n factors through P ×^G G_n (pushforward along G → G_n, merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3 NonabelianH1.map and §1.16), a G_n-map of G_n-torsors, hence an isomorphism (§1.15 Torsor.hom_isIso).

(e) Pullback of affine schemes is tensor product of coordinate rings, and tensor product commutes with directed colimits. (f) is the universal property of the limit together with equivariance at each finite stage.

(g) Q_n is an fpqc G_n-torsor. It is representable by a T-scheme affine over T, by effective fpqc descent of affine morphisms (Stacks 0245; merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1), and it is finite locally free and surjective over T because these properties descend. So Q_n → T is an fppf covering that trivializes Q_n. The map Q → lim Q_n is a G-map of G-torsors by (d), hence an isomorphism; Talpo–Vistoli sketch this direction in Remark 3.9.

Formation of P∞ commutes with arbitrary base change, and restriction to factorial indices gives the same limit. nodes.title: The genuine infinite affine quotient equivalence
nodes.statement: For any commutative ring A and f∈A, the fpqc stack of coherent native roots of (O,f) is equivalent over Spec A to [Spec C_A(f)/D_A(Q/Z)]. A quotient object over T is a represented fpqc G_T-torsor with an equivariant chart map. The equivalence retains arrows, finite projections, all transition comparisons, and arbitrary base change. For a general line bundle with section, these equivalences glue over target-line trivializations. With these LEFT coframe conventions a root-line scalar automorphism ζ acts on coframes by ζ^−1, so the quotient comparison inverts the usual scalar band on the zero-section gerbe. The infinite quotient is not claimed algebraic of finite presentation.
hypotheses: Positive exponents of arbitrary characteristic; no regularity, reducedness or log-chart hypothesis on f.
Use LEFT torsors and LEFT chart scaling throughout.
proofSteps: Send a root system to its normalized coframe-limit torsor and evaluation map. Root arrows induce the corresponding equivariant torsor maps.

Conversely extend a G-torsor to each μn. On P_n, the equivariant coordinate x_n gives a root line by descent of P_n×A1 under the diagonal LEFT action (p,a)↦(ζp,ζa), a section represented by (p,x_n(p)), and the nth-power identification represented by a^n. The relation β^−1(a) explains this convention.

The finite projection comparisons give the root α and their cocycles. Reconstruct coframes and root lines to obtain the two natural inverse isomorphisms; verify them on the fpqc trivializing torsor and descend.

Use the supplied base-change and tensor comparisons to check every finite evaluation and to glue over changes of target-line trivialization. The quotient stack is the generic Stack.quotient of the merged SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21 on the fpqc site, for the action groupoid of G on Spec C_A(f). Talpo–Vistoli's Corollary 3.13 with the Kato chart ℕ → A, 1 ↦ f already gives this equivalence for every f; the proof here makes both inverse functors explicit on native objects.

nodes.title: Isomorphism detection for coherent torsor towers
nodes.statement: Two coherent finite μn-torsor towers over k are isomorphic as towers if their torsors have the same class at every degree. Their compatible isomorphism set, when nonempty, is a torsor under G(k)=lim μn(k). For any fpqc G-torsor its automorphism sheaf is G_k, and its k-automorphism group is G(k). Class equality detects existence of a compatible arrow, not uniqueness.

proofSteps: At degree n, the isomorphism set is nonempty by class equality and is a torsor under μn(k), hence finite with at most n elements (card_rootsOfUnity). This uses actual torsor isomorphisms even when neither torsor has a k-point.

nodes.title: A Kummer limit torsor without fppf trivialization
nodes.statement: Over Q, the coherent finite torsors P_n=Spec Q[z_n]/(z_n^n−2), with z_n=z_m^(m/n), have an affine fpqc limit P under G_Q. No nonempty fppf Q-scheme U admits a section of P×U→U. Thus P is an actual fpqc torsor that is not fppf locally trivial, even though every P_n is fppf locally trivial.
hypotheses: All positive degrees; finite exponents are invertible over Q.
The existing degree bound for roots of 2 in a finite extension is imported.
proofSteps: Each P_n is the finite μn Kummer torsor for the unit 2 and its quotient maps form an actual coherent tower. RS.2/flat-torsor-tower-limit gives the affine fpqc G-torsor P.

If a nonempty fppf U trivializes P, choose a nonempty affine open Spec B of U with B a finitely generated ℚ-algebra and a maximal ideal m of B. By Zariski's lemma (finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing) K = B/m is finite over ℚ, and the section restricts to compatible nth roots of 2 in K.
The imported Eisenstein/minimal-polynomial bound n≤[K:Q] contradicts a degree n>[K:Q]. Local finite presentation of U is essential to this closed-point argument.
